answer: Continuous resource draw at a jetty. Each identity must hold a live, physically-delivered utility connection, metered at the boundary and reconciled against a signed pearl harvest log, before its key is admitted to the routing layer. A single operator cannot fake simultaneous consumption across thousands of addresses because the meter reads real draw, tying each identity to distinct upstream capacity. Cloning now costs the attacker a separate metered feed and a willow-thin audit trail per clone, paid in installation and standing capacity.
